card.headline: Other ways to say "yes"
card.sub: 20 better answers with pictures and examples

beats.speech: Looking for other ways to say yes in English? Here are twenty better answers: for friends, for requests, for agreeing, and for invitations. Each one comes with a picture and an example. Let's start.

beats.label: with friends
beats.speech: Part 1. Five relaxed answers for friends and family.

card.headline: Sure
card.example: "Can I borrow your pen?" "Sure, here you go."

beats.speech: Sure. It is a relaxed, friendly yes. "Can I borrow your pen?" "Sure, here you go."

card.headline: Yeah
card.example: "Are you coming tonight?" "Yeah, see you at eight."

beats.speech: Yeah. It means yes, in relaxed conversation. "Are you coming tonight?" "Yeah, see you at eight."

card.headline: Yep
card.example: "Did you lock the door?" "Yep, all done."

beats.speech: Yep. It is a short, quick yes. "Did you lock the door?" "Yep, all done."

card.headline: Okay
card.example: "Let's meet at six." "Okay, six is fine."

beats.speech: Okay. It means yes, I accept that. "Let's meet at six." "Okay, six is fine."

card.headline: You bet
card.example: "Can you save me a seat?" "You bet."

beats.speech: You bet. It means yes, gladly. It is informal and American. "Can you save me a seat?" "You bet."

card.headline: Which answer fits?
card.question: "Can I borrow your pen?" "___, here you go."
card.answer: "Can I borrow your pen?" "Sure, here you go."

beats.speech: Which answer fits? Can I borrow your pen? Blank, here you go. Sure or sorry? | Sure, here you go.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Sure, here you go.
Yeah, see you at eight.
Yep, all done.
Okay, six is fine.
You bet.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Sure, here you go. | Yeah, see you at eight. | Yep, all done. | Okay, six is fine. | You bet.

beats.label: to a request
beats.speech: Part 2. Five polite answers when someone asks you for something.

card.headline: Of course
card.meaning: yes, and I am happy to do it
card.example: "Could you open the window?" "Of course."

beats.speech: Of course. It means yes, and I am happy to do it. "Could you open the window?" "Of course."

card.headline: Certainly
card.example: "Could I have the bill, please?" "Certainly, sir."

beats.speech: Certainly. It is a polite, formal yes. "Could I have the bill, please?" "Certainly, sir."

card.headline: No problem
card.meaning: yes, it is easy for me
card.example: "Can you send me the file?" "No problem, I'll send it now."

beats.speech: No problem. It means yes, it is easy for me. "Can you send me the file?" "No problem, I'll send it now."

card.headline: By all means
card.example: "May I sit here?" "By all means."

beats.speech: By all means. It means yes, please do. Use it to give permission. "May I sit here?" "By all means."

card.headline: Gladly
card.example: "Would you help me carry these bags?" "Gladly."

beats.speech: Gladly. It means yes, with pleasure. "Would you help me carry these bags?" "Gladly."

card.headline: Which answer fits?
card.question: "Could I have the bill, please?" "___, sir."
card.answer: "Could I have the bill, please?" "Certainly, sir."

beats.speech: Which answer fits? Could I have the bill, please? Blank, sir. Certainly or yep? | Certainly, sir.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Of course.
Certainly, sir.
No problem, I'll send it now.
By all means.
Gladly.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Of course. | Certainly, sir. | No problem, I'll send it now. | By all means. | Gladly.

beats.label: when you agree
beats.speech: Part 3. Five strong answers when you fully agree.

card.headline: Absolutely
card.example: "Was the film worth seeing?" "Absolutely, it was brilliant."

beats.speech: Absolutely. It means yes, completely. "Was the film worth seeing?" "Absolutely, it was brilliant."

card.headline: Definitely
card.example: "Will you come to the wedding?" "Definitely, I wouldn't miss it."

beats.speech: Definitely. It means yes, without any doubt. "Will you come to the wedding?" "Definitely, I wouldn't miss it."

card.headline: Exactly
card.meaning: yes, that is just what I mean
card.example: "So we need more time?" "Exactly."

beats.speech: Exactly. It means yes, that is just what I mean. "So we need more time?" "Exactly."

card.headline: Totally
card.example: "This song is great." "Totally, I love it."

beats.speech: Totally. It means yes, I completely agree. It is informal. "This song is great." "Totally, I love it."

card.headline: For sure
card.example: "Is it going to rain?" "For sure, look at those clouds."

beats.speech: For sure. It means yes, certainly. It is informal. "Is it going to rain?" "For sure, look at those clouds."

card.headline: Which answer fits?
card.question: "So we need more time?" "___. Two more days."
card.answer: "So we need more time?" "Exactly. Two more days."

beats.speech: Which answer fits? So we need more time? Blank. Two more days. Exactly or never? | Exactly. Two more days.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Absolutely, it was brilliant.
Definitely, I wouldn't miss it.
Exactly.
Totally, I love it.
For sure, look at those clouds.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Absolutely, it was brilliant. | Definitely, I wouldn't miss it. | Exactly. | Totally, I love it. | For sure, look at those clouds.

beats.label: plans and invitations
beats.speech: Part 4. Five ways to say yes to a plan or an invitation.

card.headline: Sounds good
card.example: "Pizza tonight?" "Sounds good."

beats.speech: Sounds good. It means yes, I like that plan. "Pizza tonight?" "Sounds good."

card.headline: Good idea
card.meaning: yes, that is a smart suggestion
card.example: "Shall we take a taxi?" "Good idea, it's late."

beats.speech: Good idea. It means yes, that is a smart suggestion. "Shall we take a taxi?" "Good idea, it's late."

card.headline: Works for me
card.meaning: yes, that time or plan suits me
card.example: "Is Friday at ten all right?" "Works for me."

beats.speech: Works for me. It means yes, that time or plan suits me. "Is Friday at ten all right?" "Works for me."

card.headline: Count me in
card.example: "We're playing football on Sunday." "Count me in."

beats.speech: Count me in. It means yes, I want to join. "We're playing football on Sunday." "Count me in."

card.headline: I would love to
card.example: "Would you like to come to dinner?" "I would love to."

beats.speech: I would love to. It means yes, with great pleasure. People often shorten it to I'd love to. "Would you like to come to dinner?" "I would love to."

card.headline: Which answer fits?
card.question: "We're playing football on Sunday." "___! What time?"
card.answer: "We're playing football on Sunday." "Count me in! What time?"

beats.speech: Which answer fits? We're playing football on Sunday. Blank! What time? Count me in, or no thanks? | Count me in! What time?

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Sounds good.
Good idea, it's late.
Works for me.
Count me in.
I would love to.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Sounds good. | Good idea, it's late. | Works for me. | Count me in. | I would love to.

card.headline: Which answer will you use today?

beats.speech: That's twenty ways to say yes. Which one will you use today? Write it in the comments.
